beats.label: S1 · Red Moon
beats.text: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov beats Apollo 11 to the Moon in 1969, humiliating NASA and turning the space race into an open-ended contest America cannot afford to lose.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the whole alt-history premise; every subsequent political and technical push in the show flows from the Soviets winning.

beats.label: S1 · Nixon's Women
beats.text: After the Soviets land the first woman on the Moon, NASA scrambles to enlist female astronauts — Tracy Stevens, Molly Cobb, Ellen Waverly and Danielle Poole all make the cut.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the four women who anchor almost every future season.

beats.label: S1 · Ice at Shackleton
beats.text: Rappelling into a lunar crater on Apollo 15, Molly Cobb finds water ice — the resource NASA needs to build the permanent Jamestown base that opens two years later.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Jamestown, the setting for S1–S2 and the strategic prize both superpowers fight over.

beats.label: S1 · Apollo 23
beats.text: Apollo 23 explodes on the pad, killing eleven; von Braun reveals political sabotage caused it, and Margo uses that evidence to blackmail her way into flight director.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains Margo's grip on NASA — the power base she keeps through S4.

beats.label: S1 · Broken Gordo
beats.text: Isolation at Jamestown cracks Gordo Stevens's mind; Danielle Poole snaps her own arm to smuggle him home, hiding his breakdown but grounding him indefinitely.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the Stevens family fragility and Danielle's quiet self-sacrifice, both of which pay off in S2.

beats.label: S1 · Shane
beats.text: After a fight with Karen, Ed's son Shane sneaks out and is killed in a car accident, gutting the Baldwins' marriage while Ed is commanding from the Moon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The wound that defines Ed and Karen going forward and drives every later choice about Kelly.

beats.label: S1 · Rescue and 1983
beats.text: Apollo 24 is stranded in deep space; Ed's rescue costs Deke Slayton's life. By 1983 the Sea Dragon is ferrying plutonium to a rapidly expanding Jamestown.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Time-jumps into the militarised world S2 opens in.

cliffhanger.text: The Baldwins have buried their son and Gordo has been silently shattered, yet a decade on both Jamestown and the Cold War have only grown, with plutonium now flying to the Moon.
questions: How has a militarised Jamestown reshaped life on Earth after ten years?
Will Gordo ever recover enough to fly again, and does anyone at NASA still trust him?
Can Ed and Karen's marriage survive Shane's death, or has grief already broken it?

characters.name: Edward 'Ed' Baldwin
characters.line: Apollo 15 commander and Jamestown pioneer, now chief astronaut whose son Shane died while he was on the Moon.

characters.name: Karen Baldwin
characters.line: Ed's wife, running the astronauts' Outpost bar and shattered by Shane's death.

characters.name: Gordo Stevens
characters.line: Astronaut broken by Jamestown isolation; smuggled home by Danielle's fake injury and quietly grounded.

characters.name: Tracy Stevens
characters.line: Gordo's wife, one of NASA's first female astronauts and increasingly the family's public face.

characters.name: Molly Cobb
characters.line: Blunt Apollo 15 astronaut who found the lunar water ice that made a permanent Jamestown possible.

characters.name: Danielle Poole
characters.line: Astronaut and Jamestown veteran who broke her own arm to cover Gordo's mental collapse.

characters.name: Ellen Waverly
characters.line: Closeted lesbian astronaut who married her friend Larry after FBI scrutiny of her private life.

characters.name: Margo Madison
characters.line: Steel-nerved engineer who blackmailed her way to flight director using the real cause of Apollo 23.

beats.label: S2 · Solar Storm
beats.text: A solar storm hits the Moon; Molly Cobb saves colleague Wubbo from lethal radiation but absorbs enough herself to trigger an incurable glaucoma diagnosis.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants Molly's slow blinding, which reshapes her role by season's end.

beats.label: S2 · Pathfinder & Soyuz
beats.text: Ed takes command of the new nuclear shuttle Pathfinder; Danielle Poole demands and wins the historic Apollo–Soyuz command opposite the Soviets.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits Ed and Danielle onto the two missions that collide at the climax and reset their careers.

beats.label: S2 · Margo & Sergei
beats.text: Behind the mission, Margo and Soviet engineer Sergei secretly co-design the docking hardware — a genuine friendship the KGB is quietly weaponising against her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the Margo–Sergei entanglement that drives every subsequent season.

beats.label: S2 · KAL 007
beats.text: Korean Air 007 is shot down with NASA administrator Paine aboard; Ellen becomes acting director as her closeted marriage to Larry cages her rising political future.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Ellen on the ladder to real power and locks in the personal cost that catches up to her later.

beats.label: S2 · Guns on the Moon
beats.text: Marines carry rifles to Jamestown to retake a mining site the Soviets bugged; a botched confrontation kills one cosmonaut and puts both superpowers on lunar hair-trigger.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The escalation that makes the finale's shooting war inevitable.

beats.label: S2 · The Stevens Die
beats.text: Cosmonauts storm Jamestown; Gordo and Tracy Stevens patch a damaged reactor from outside in duct-tape suits, saving the base but dying together in vacuum.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes both Stevens parents; every future Stevens beat is about the hole they left.

beats.label: S2 · Standoff and Mars
beats.text: In lunar orbit, Ed refuses to fire Pathfinder's missiles and destroys the American Sea Dragon instead — averting nuclear war. A coda leaps to 1995: a boot on Mars.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the next arena and the tone shift into S3.

cliffhanger.text: Nuclear war has been averted and Jamestown rebuilds, but Gordo and Tracy are dead, Karen has slept with their son Danny, the KGB still holds Margo through Sergei, and by 1995 boots are already on Mars.
questions: Who reached Mars first, and how does the race look a decade after the lunar standoff?
Can Margo keep feeding the Soviets what they demand without being caught?
What happens to Ed and Karen's marriage now that she has slept with Gordo's son?

characters.name: Edward 'Ed' Baldwin
characters.line: Chief astronaut turned Pathfinder commander who defused the lunar standoff by destroying the Sea Dragon.

characters.name: Karen Baldwin
characters.line: Sold the Outpost, slept once with Gordo's son Danny, and now confronting Ed with the truth.

characters.name: Danielle Poole
characters.line: Back at the top, commanded the historic Apollo–Soyuz handshake in orbit.

characters.name: Ellen Wilson
characters.line: Closeted acting NASA administrator whose lover Pam left her to keep her political future clear.

characters.name: Molly Cobb
characters.line: Chief of the astronaut office, secretly going blind from her solar-storm radiation exposure.

characters.name: Margo Madison
characters.line: NASA flight director being played by the KGB through her friendship with Sergei.

characters.name: Sergei Nikulov
characters.line: Soviet engineer with real affection for Margo but under KGB orders to extract NASA secrets.

characters.name: Aleida Rosales
characters.line: Adult NASA engineer newly hired onto Apollo–Soyuz, tentatively reconnecting with Margo.

characters.name: Kelly Baldwin
characters.line: Ed and Karen's adopted teenage daughter, heading to the Naval Academy at Annapolis.

characters.name: Danny Stevens
characters.line: Gordo and Tracy's older son, a naval officer whose one night with Karen he cannot let go.

beats.label: S3 · Polaris Falls
beats.text: Space junk cripples the Polaris hotel; Sam Cleveland dies, Ed is injured, and Dev Ayesa's Helios buys the wreck to sprint the private sector to Mars.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Brings in Dev and Helios, the new dominant force reshaping the race.

beats.label: S3 · Three Ships to Mars
beats.text: A three-way Mars race launches for 1994. Margo overrides Molly to give NASA's command to Danielle; Ed jumps to Helios and commands Phoenix instead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the American-Soviet-Helios triangle that structures the whole season.

beats.label: S3 · Margo Cornered
beats.text: The KGB threatens Sergei's life until Margo hands over NASA's nuclear engine design; Aleida, newly NASA flight director, quietly begins to suspect her mentor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the Margo–Aleida rupture that becomes the season's endgame.

beats.label: S3 · Happy Valley
beats.text: Sojourner reaches Mars first; Danielle and Soviet cosmonaut Kuznetsov tie for the first bootprint. Helios lands nearby, and all three crews share the Happy Valley base.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why one shared Mars base exists at the start of every future season.

beats.label: S3 · Danny's Sabotage
beats.text: Obsessed with Karen, Danny Stevens sabotages a Mars drill that kills Kelly's Soviet lover Alexei — whose emergency transfusion reveals Kelly is pregnant with his child.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Creates Ed's grandson and the guilt that will define Ed's relationship with Danny.

beats.label: S3 · Ellen Comes Out
beats.text: Ellen, now US president, comes out publicly to defuse Larry's affair scandal. Jimmy Stevens's radical friends then bomb Johnson Space Center, killing Karen Baldwin and Molly Cobb.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Karen and Molly and ends Ellen's era; Ed is left alone with Mars.

beats.label: S3 · Exile and Defection
beats.text: Danny confesses his sabotage and is exiled to a North Korean capsule on Mars; Margo secretly defects to the USSR to escape the FBI, quietly resurfacing in Moscow by 2003.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two exits that define the world S4 opens in.

cliffhanger.text: Karen and Molly are dead, Danny is broken and exiled on Mars, Kelly is raising a newborn son by the late Alexei, and Margo — the head of NASA — has secretly vanished into the USSR.
questions: What has become of Margo living inside the Soviet Union eight years later?
Can Ed, still on Mars, ever be reconciled with what Danny did — and what happens to Danny in exile?
Will Aleida ever confront what Margo did, now that she is running mission control alone?

characters.name: Edward 'Ed' Baldwin
characters.line: Jumped to Helios to command Phoenix, now stranded on Mars, mourning Karen and betrayed by Danny.

characters.name: Danielle Poole
characters.line: NASA's Mars commander and first American on the surface, returning to Earth as a hero.

characters.name: Kelly Baldwin
characters.line: Ed's daughter, newly a mother to Alexei's son after her pre-eclampsia scare on Phoenix.

characters.name: Margo Madison
characters.line: Former NASA director who secretly defected to the USSR to escape an FBI espionage investigation.

characters.name: Aleida Rosales
characters.line: New NASA flight director who suspects Margo betrayed the engine design but does not yet know why.

characters.name: Dev Ayesa
characters.line: Brash Helios founder pushed out of his own company after the Mars race's chaos.

characters.name: Danny Stevens
characters.line: Gordo's addict son, exiled to an abandoned North Korean capsule on Mars after confessing his sabotage.

characters.name: Sergei Nikulov
characters.line: Defected to the US with his family after the KGB's leverage on Margo destroyed his life.

characters.name: Lee Jung-Gil
characters.line: Solo North Korean astronaut stranded on Mars since 1995, now living quietly at Happy Valley.

beats.label: S4 · Tremors and a Death
beats.text: An asteroid capture goes wrong in 2003, killing Kuznetsov and revealing Ed Baldwin's worsening hand tremors. Danielle Poole is coaxed back to command Happy Valley.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Ed's medical decline and puts Danielle back in charge, framing the season.

beats.label: S4 · Miles Dale
beats.text: Unemployed rig worker Miles Dale takes a Mars contract instead of Moon work; underpaid and misled, he joins Happy Valley's thriving black market.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the working-class Mars audience surrogate the whole rebellion arc runs through.

beats.label: S4 · Irina's Asset
beats.text: In the USSR, Margo lives under quiet surveillance until Irina, the new Roscosmos director, pulls her back into space work as her rehabilitated Soviet asset.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Irina, S4's chief antagonist, and re-arms Margo as a public player.

beats.label: S4 · Goldilocks
beats.text: An iridium-rich asteroid, Goldilocks, is found near Mars. Margo returns to Houston under diplomatic immunity to design its capture — worth trillions to both superpowers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The MacGuffin that reunites Margo and Aleida and drives every faction in the finale.

beats.label: S4 · Grounded, and Danny
beats.text: Ed's tremors are exposed; Danielle strips him of flight status. Flashbacks show her visits to exiled Danny, who quietly takes his own life on the Martian surface.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Danny for good and pushes Ed toward Dev's off-books plot.

beats.label: S4 · Sergei Murdered
beats.text: Sergei warns Margo that Irina orchestrated their friendship for years — then is murdered and staged as suicide. Dev enlists Ed in a plot to hijack Goldilocks into Mars orbit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The betrayal that turns Margo against Irina, and the trigger for the hijack.

beats.label: S4 · Stolen to Mars
beats.text: Margo and Aleida secretly sabotage NASA control; the hijackers pull Goldilocks into Mars orbit. Margo takes the fall alone and is arrested; by 2012 the rock is a thriving mine.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reshapes the Mars economy and Margo's future — the world S5 inherits.

cliffhanger.text: Mars kept its stolen asteroid and by 2012 has become an economic linchpin, but Margo is in a US prison, Sergei is dead by Irina's hand, and Kuznetsov Station now dominates a much bigger colony no one on Earth can quite control.
questions: With Margo behind bars, does she stay silent about who really executed the Goldilocks hijack?
Who is running Mars now that 5,000 people live under the shadow of Kuznetsov Station?
Can Irina, exposed inside Roscosmos, hold on to power — and what does she want from Mars next?

characters.name: Edward 'Ed' Baldwin
characters.line: Still on Mars a decade later, forced out of command by his hand tremors and pulled into Dev's asteroid hijack.

characters.name: Danielle Poole
characters.line: Returned to command Happy Valley, wounded in the riot and finally heading home to Earth.

characters.name: Kelly Baldwin
characters.line: On Mars with her young son Alex, running Helios-funded biology research alongside Aleida.

characters.name: Alex Baldwin
characters.line: Kelly's young son by the late Alexei, growing up around Ed on Mars.

characters.name: Margo Madison
characters.line: Exposed defector who took sole blame for the Goldilocks hijack and is now in a US prison.

characters.name: Aleida Rosales
characters.line: NASA flight director who secretly co-sabotaged control to steer the asteroid to Mars.

characters.name: Dev Ayesa
characters.line: Helios founder who orchestrated the asteroid hijack from Mars.

characters.name: Miles Dale
characters.line: Former oil rig worker turned Happy Valley black-market kingpin, freed during the riot.

characters.name: Irina Morozova
characters.line: Roscosmos director who groomed Margo for years and had Sergei killed to keep her leverage.

characters.name: Lee Jung-Gil
characters.line: North Korean commander at Happy Valley, quiet ally to the hijackers.

beats.label: S5 · Mars 2012
beats.text: By 2012 Mars houses 5,000, including illegal 'craters'. Dying of cancer, Ed runs an independence movement while his grandson Alex discovers a murdered ISN worker.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the timeline, Ed's terminal condition, and the murder that fractures the colony's politics.

beats.label: S5 · Jung-Gil to ISN
beats.text: Jung-Gil is arrested for the murder despite a Russian cover-up. Ed smuggles him to the ISN base, which grants asylum — inflaming Happy Valley's factions.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cracks open the Mars-6 versus ISN split that structures the rebellion.

beats.label: S5 · Ed Dies
beats.text: Aleida wins Kelly the Titan biology mission on the revived Sojourner-1. Ed dies of cancer with Alex at his bedside as Kelly departs for Titan.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the show's spine and launches the mission that closes it.

beats.label: S5 · The Leak
beats.text: Alex leaks Dev's plan to automate Happy Valley and expel 98% of workers. Strikes erupt into a curfew crackdown, and peacekeepers open fire on a protest.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The single spark for every subsequent act of violence in the season.

beats.label: S5 · Rebellion and Embargo
beats.text: Armed workers seize Mars government; Irina joins them and cuts iridium exports. President Bragg answers with a full embargo and dispatches Marines to retake the colony.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Formalises the rebellion and puts the invading military force on its way.

beats.label: S5 · Domes and Titan
beats.text: Peacekeepers destroy Happy Valley's farm domes as Sojourner lands manually on Titan. Marines land on Mars firing wildly; Alex accidentally shoots one of the invaders.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Twin climaxes: Mars starves and shoots itself, Titan is reached.

beats.label: S5 · Independence
beats.text: Kelly stays on Titan so her crew can escape, dying as she finds microbial life. Mars gains independence; a 2020 coda shows the derelict Mars-94 mysteriously reactivating.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The finale itself — closes the human arcs and leaves the audience with the reactivation mystery.

cliffhanger.text: Mars is a free world at last, but bought at the cost of Ed, Kelly, and thousands of lives — and eight years later, the wreck of a lost Soviet mission has quietly powered itself back on.
questions: What or who is reactivating the long-derelict Mars-94 in 2020?
Can an independent Mars survive without Ed, Kelly, or Earth's industrial support?
Does the microbial life Kelly touched on Titan change what humanity now believes it is?

characters.name: Kelly Baldwin
characters.line: Ed's daughter and Titan mission commander, dying alone after discovering microbial life so her crew could live.

characters.name: Edward 'Ed' Baldwin
characters.line: Died of cancer on Mars, having founded the independence movement his descendants finished.

characters.name: Aleida Rosales
characters.line: CEO of Helios, sped Kelly's Titan mission and quietly aided the Mars rebellion.

characters.name: Dev Ayesa
characters.line: Helios strategist whose Mars automation plan sparked the uprising.

characters.name: Alex Baldwin
characters.line: Kelly's teenage son, radicalised by the leak and Ed's death and drawn into the independence militia.

characters.name: Irina Morozova
characters.line: Former Roscosmos director who joined the Mars rebels after fleeing a collapsing USSR.

characters.name: Miles Dale
characters.line: Happy Valley black-market veteran turned rebel negotiator.

characters.name: Lee Jung-Gil
characters.line: North Korean defector at ISN whose arrest first cracked open the crisis.
